title: Task Scheduler
description: Find the minimum number of intervals needed to run all tasks with a cooldown using a frequency-based greedy formula.

data.text: You are given a list of CPU tasks as characters and a non-negative cooldown `n`. Identical tasks must be separated by at least `n` intervals. In each interval the CPU may run one task or stay idle. Return the minimum number of intervals needed to finish all tasks.

**Input:** `tasks = ["A","A","A","B","B","B"]`, `n = 2`

**Output:** `8`

**Explanation:** One valid schedule is `A B _ A B _ A B`.

The most frequent task is the bottleneck. If it appears `maxFreq` times, those occurrences need `maxFreq - 1` gaps between them, and each gap must be at least `n` slots wide. Filling those frames gives the schedule its shape; other tasks either fit inside the frames or extend the total beyond them.

data.title: Formula — O(n) with counting
data.content: Count frequencies, find maxFreq and how many tasks tie for it.

data.title: The Math.Max is the whole trick
data.text: When many distinct tasks exist, filler tasks occupy the idle slots completely and the answer is simply the number of tasks. When few distinct tasks exist, idle slots are unavoidable and the frame formula wins. Taking the max of the two covers both cases with one expression.

data.title: Why 'maxCount' is added, not n
data.text: The final frame holds one occurrence of each task that reaches `maxFreq`, so its width is `maxCount`, not the full frame size `n + 1`. Using `n` here is the most common wrong answer.

If the formula feels like magic, simulate round by round: take up to `n + 1` distinct tasks with the highest remaining counts from a max-heap, decrement them, and re-add the survivors. The simulation takes O(total · log 26) and produces the same answer, which makes it a useful correctness check.

data.title: Simulation with a max-heap
data.content: Round-based scheduling makes the cooldown rule explicit.

data.caption: The most frequent task defines frames of width n+1; the last frame only needs one slot per remaining task.
data.definition:
graph TD
    A["maxFreq = 3 (A), n = 2"] --> B["frame 1: A B _"]
    B --> C["frame 2: A B _"]
    C --> D["final frame: A B"]
    D --> E["total = 2 * 3 + 2 = 8"]
    E --> F["max(8, 6 tasks) = 8"]
    style F fill:#e8f5e9,stroke:#2e7d32

data.title: Complete solution
data.content: In an interview, state the frame reasoning first, then confirm the answer with the simulation if time allows. The formula is what interviewers expect; the simulation is how you convince yourself it is right.
